messages:
maria: Morning — MiraHealth weekly-ish check-in. Pulled last 24h: 1.2M requests, overall error rate 0.9% (baseline ~0.3%). Notable: 5xx burst around 03:10–03:25 UTC and sustained rate-limit events during peak traffic.

nate: I dug into infra traces — there's a ~45s window where RT latency jumped and we saw amplified 502s from the streaming cluster. Looks correlated with a client fanout spike. :warning:

jordan: Quick breakdown I ran from logs (filtered by acct=MiraHealth):
```
count by status_code, path from logs where timestamp >= -24h and account = "MiraHealth"
results: 502 -> 6,200 (0.52%), 504 -> 1,800 (0.15%), 429 -> 3,400 (0.28%)
Top paths (by 5xx): /v1/chat/stream -> 3,900, /v1/generate -> 2,100, /v1/embeddings -> 1,000
```

ashley: FYI I already notified MiraHealth AMs. They're on a heavy ingestion job today — they expected a spike but didn't expect 5xx. Scheduling a sync at 16:30 PT to go over retries/backoff.

maria: Good. Two quick asks: (1) can we validate whether our prefix cache/kv eviction kicked in during the burst? (2) can we confirm client-side retry behavior (they might be retrying aggressively and amplifying load)?

nate: On (1) — cache hit rates dropped ~30% for the chat cluster during the window; eviction due to mem pressure on node-gpux-07. I can repro with the trace: heavy long-context requests caused larger KV footprints.

nate: On (2) — sampled request headers show retries: X-Retry-Count >=3 in ~18% of failing requests. They use a 1s fixed backoff. We should recommend exponential jitter.

jordan: Also saw spike in 429s across the account buckets starting 14:00 UTC — looks like client hitting per-route rate limits, not global quota. Config: MiraHealth has high concurrency but some endpoints (chat/stream) still using default per-route caps.

ops-bot: alert: rate_limit_fired account=MiraHealth route=/v1/chat/stream window=60s count=980 threshold=500

ashley: Actioning: enablement call to include recommended retry headers + guidance on concurrency. I'll send draft notes before the sync.

maria: Ops actions: nate — open a postmortem-lite with timeline + mem pressure metrics, prioritize KV GC tuning for streaming nodes. jordan — produce quick config diff to raise per-route caps for this account (we can gate behind quota checks).

nate: Created ticket CS-4387 with initial timeline and logs link: https://redwood.internal/ops/tickets/CS-4387. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

jordan: Draft rate-limit tweak (tested in staging): increase chat/stream per-route window from 500->1200 for MiraHealth only; add adaptive token bucket to avoid burst collapse. Will attach test logs.

maria: Customer-facing summary for the AMs (short): "We saw a blended impact of streaming KV eviction and client-side aggressive retries. Root cause likely client fanout + memory pressure leading to 502/504; separate 429s from hitting per-route caps. Next steps: tune KV GC, adjust per-route cap, and advise exponential jitter on retries. AM: schedule 16:30 PT sync." :thumbsup:

ashley: I'll send that note and invite eng on the call.

maria: Any objections to a temporary per-account bump while we do KV tuning? We want to avoid immediate churn in production.

nate: No objections. We'll monitor for downstream effects. I'll add canary filters and rollback knobs.

jordan: I'll push the config change to canary by 15:40 UTC and watch error rate.

maria: Perfect. Closing loop here — will add a short post-check note in this thread after the canary completes. Thanks all.

ashley: noted.

ops-bot: deploybot: config-change to canary complete (jordan) at 15:41 UTC.

maria: Post-check: after canary, 5xxs dropped ~65% on canary nodes, 429s reduced by ~50% for the account. Leaving open until full rollout tonight.
